kit/ai — NPC verbs and the wave director

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Host decisions and replicated NPC statePerceptionSteering (per tick; returns the new position)The wave directorWorked example: the dweller's brainDirector and presentation constraints

Use kit/ai to find targets, steer NPCs, and schedule enemy waves. The game implements the decisions about when an NPC should chase, flee, or patrol; the package provides perception, movement, and wave-scheduling helpers.

The examples here use coop replication: the host makes NPC decisions and streams their positions as the entity owner. On the sim lane, an NPC instead has predict fields, advances in server ticks, and makes decisions in the authority pass. The pure perception and steering math works in either model. The wave director also remains authority-side logic. See nav for restrictions on live NavigationServer queries during replay.

Host decisions and replicated NPC state#

The game owns the NPC update loop. kit/ai provides no Brain type or behavior tree. Cavecrawl's dweller uses a switch in its host tick to choose behavior and writes the result to a replicated state: u8.

In this coop setup, the host player owns the NPC entity. The host's decision procedure writes x/y, and clients interpolate those owner-streamed positions. The NPC's state byte and hp use ordinary replication. Cavecrawl declares that state in examples/cavecrawl/scripts/dweller.odin:

Odin
Dweller :: struct {
	owner:  gd.Node2d,
	glyph:  gd.Label `gd:"onready=Glyph"`,
	net_id: knet.Net_Id,
	x, y:   f32 `gd:"owner"`, // continuous owner fields interpolate by default
	hp:     i32 `gd:"replicate"`,
	state:  u8 `gd:"replicate"`, // behavior state displayed by every peer
	...
}

Clients use state to display the NPC's behavior and interpolate its streamed position. Only the host runs the decision loop, so clients need presentation code without a separate AI loop or NPC packet format.

The package's math is deterministic, allocation-free, and independent of Godot. Positions use [3]f32; 2D games leave z at zero.

Perception#

Odin
Target :: struct {
	id:  u32,
	pos: [3]f32,
}

// Return whether geometry blocks the line from `from` to `to`.
// The game supplies geometry queries; nil treats the world as unobstructed.
Blocker_Proc :: proc(user: rawptr, from, to: [3]f32) -> bool

// The nearest target within `max_range` that line-of-sight reaches.
nearest :: proc(from: [3]f32, targets: []Target, max_range: f32, blocker: Blocker_Proc = nil, user: rawptr = nil) -> (best: Target, ok: bool)

in_reach :: proc "contextless" (from, to: [3]f32, reach: f32) -> bool

Steering (per tick; returns the new position)#

Odin
// Move toward `goal` for one tick. `arrived` reports reaching it.
// The final step lands exactly on the goal without overshooting.
step_toward :: proc "contextless" (pos, goal: [3]f32, speed: f32) -> (next: [3]f32, arrived: bool)

// Move away from `threat` for one tick. When position equals the
// threat position, use +x as the fallback direction.
step_away :: proc "contextless" (pos, threat: [3]f32, speed: f32) -> [3]f32

// Patrol bookkeeping: advance (and wrap) the waypoint index once the current
// one is within `reach`. The game steps toward `points[current]` as usual.
patrol_next :: proc "contextless" (points: [][3]f32, current: int, pos: [3]f32, reach: f32) -> int

Speeds are per tick. To walk a navmesh instead of a straight line, feed step_toward the goal from kit/nav's next_point.

The wave director#

The wave director schedules spawns from a list of wave counts and rest times. The game chooses each NPC type and spawn position when the director emits a spawn. Only one wave runs at a time. The next starts after all NPCs in the current wave die and its rest interval has elapsed.

Odin
Wave :: struct {
	count: u16, // how many this wave
	rest:  u16, // rest ticks after this wave clears and before the next
}

Director :: struct {
	wave:       int, // waves fully started so far (1-based once running)
	pending:    u16, // still to spawn in the current wave
	alive:      int, // living spawns (the game reports deaths)
	rest_until: u64, // tick when the next wave may start
	done:       bool, // all waves started and cleared
}

// Call once per host tick. Returns the number of NPCs to spawn this tick.
// The director limits spawning to one per tick to spread replication work.
director_tick :: proc(d: ^Director, tick: u64, waves: []Wave) -> (spawn: int)

// The game reports each director-spawned NPC's death. When the wave clears,
// the rest interval before the next wave begins.
director_note_death :: proc(d: ^Director, tick: u64, waves: []Wave)

// The current wave number for HUDs ("wave 2/3"); 0 before the first.
director_wave :: proc "contextless" (d: ^Director) -> int

Worked example: the dweller's brain#

The host updates each dweller once per tick. It finds a visible target, selects a behavior with a switch, and writes the resulting position and state. Those fields carry the result to clients. The procedure is cave_dwellers_think in examples/cavecrawl/scripts/host.odin:

Odin
pos := [3]f32{dw.x, dw.y, 0}
seen, spotted := kai.nearest(pos, targets[:], DWELLER_AGGRO)

state := DWELLER_IDLE
switch {
case spotted && dw.hp <= FLEE_BELOW:
	state = DWELLER_FLEE
	pos = kai.step_away(pos, seen.pos, DWELLER_SPEED / 2)
case spotted:
	state = DWELLER_CHASE
	if kai.in_reach(pos, seen.pos, BITE_RANGE) {
		if brain.bite_cd == 0 {
			brain.bite_cd = BITE_CD
			cave_hurt_spelunker(self, victim_id, self.spelunkers[victim_id], BITE_DMG, knet.PLAYER_ID_INVALID, false)
		}
	} else {
		pos, _ = kai.step_toward(pos, seen.pos, DWELLER_SPEED)
	}
case:
	pos, _ = kai.step_toward(pos, brain.home, DWELLER_SPEED)
}
dw.x = pos.x
dw.y = pos.y
dw.state = state

The director drives spawning in the same tick, and deaths report back (cave_slay_dweller calls kai.director_note_death):

Odin
to_spawn := kai.director_tick(&self.director, u64(self.host_ticks), self.waves[:self.waves_n])
for _ in 0 ..< to_spawn {
	cave_spawn_dweller(self)
}

Apply damage and record combat stats through kit/combat's hit/credit_*. Create and remove entities through the generated typed helpers dweller_spawn, boot_spawn_send, and dweller_despawn. See the Boot entity factory.

Director and presentation constraints#

  • Call director_tick before the range expression. Odin reevaluates a range bound on each iteration. Calling director_tick there repeatedly changes director state and can drain the wave, so store its result first.
  • Call the director once per tick. It schedules one spawn per tick.
  • Keep private NPC state such as bite cooldowns and home positions in a host-side map (self.brains[id]). Replicate the results other peers need: x/y, state, and hp.
  • The host writes positions in tick-sized steps, so its node still needs frame-rate smoothing. dweller_process uses kai.step_toward with +50% slack on every role. On clients it follows the interpolated stream; on the host it smooths the discrete tick updates.
  • step_away picks +x when the position equals the threat position. nearest with a nil blocker treats the world as unobstructed.
